newsitem.title: UK: Nikko management changes stress growth.
newsitem.headline: Nikko management changes stress growth.

text.p: Japanese trading house Nikko Securities announced management changes on Monday which it said showed its ambition to accelerate international growth.
"All the appointments announced today send a clear message to everybody that Nikko is ambitious to accelerate its international growth," a statement said.
Nikko said in a statement that Masashi Kaneko would be promoted to executive deputy president.
Michel de Carvalho, joint chairman of Nikko Europe, takes responsibility with joint chairman Tadao Osada for running European operations.

De Carvalho has also been appointed global head of capital markets outside Japan, making the sector the first to have a global head and a change from its previous strategy of employees reporting on geographic lines.
Nikko said other areas, such as fixed income and equity, were expected to follow.

Nikko added that in London, it had promoted Brian Berry and Gen Yamaguchi to be joint chief executives of Nikko Europe, replacing Jun Okano who will head Nikko's Asian and Oceanic operations out of Hong Kong.
Kenji Yoshibayashi will move to London to be managing director of fixed income and money markets while Hiroyuki Fukushima will join as managing director of equity trading.

Nikko said that in Europe, it was continuing its policy of localisation with the appointment of Hiromi Kondo and Michael Gairin as joint presidents of Nikko France S.A, replacing Minoru Yamamoto who will return to Tokyo.
In Spain, Jose Nestola becomes president of the office, replacing Koji Tanaka who will move to be executive vice-president of Nikko Bank (Switzerland).
Rainer Schmitt has been appointed deputy managing director of Nikko in Frankfurt and will continue as head of the Berlin office. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
